title: Forms of Energy and the Water Cycle Unit Test
subject: science

items.prompt: State the five forms of energy and give one everyday use of each form.

points.text: Names light, heat, sound, movement and stored energy
Gives an everyday use for each form, such as a lamp giving out light or a radio giving out sound

items.prompt: A pupil says that when a lamp stops shining, its energy has been used up. Explain why this idea is wrong.

points.text: States that the energy is never used up and does not disappear
Explains that the energy changes form and moves somewhere else, like light and heat leaving the bulb

items.prompt: State the process by which liquid water changes into water vapour at the surface of a pond.

points.text: Notes it happens at the surface and needs heat from the surroundings

items.prompt: A cold mirror held above a kettle of boiling water becomes covered in droplets. Explain how the droplets form.

points.text: States water vapour from the kettle touches the cold mirror
States the vapour loses heat and condenses into liquid droplets

levels.label: Secure
levels.descriptor: Answers use the correct part and process names and link each observation to a cause.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Part and process names are mostly correct but the cause link is incomplete.

levels.label: Beginning
levels.descriptor: Part and process names are missing or confused and no cause is given.
